findings.what: "A cable, a breaker or a generator sees the current, so check its rating against S, not P" is a false absolute for a generator, which the brief's own sources rate in kVA at a stated power factor with a kW figure as well (100 kVA gives 80 kW at 0.8; the 60 Hz diesel set's 630 kVA and 504 kW at 0.8, brief notes 3.8), so reword it: a cable or a breaker follows the current, so S at a given voltage, while a generator is checked against both its kVA and its kW at the stated power factor, citing those sources.

findings.where: screen 6 (Two meters) and the lesson as a whole against the brief
findings.what: The brief's lesson 8 row promises the alternator rated "in kVA at a specified frequency and power factor" and the 630 kVA / 504 kW data sheet, and its decisions name "generator ratings" as lesson 8's above-the-maths puzzle, but neither appears; screen 6's 4.8 kW / 6 kVA is a bare 3-4-5 sum like Trigonometry lesson 8's, so a generator-rating puzzle in its place would pitch above the maths and bring the one sourced sea example this lesson was given.

findings.where: screen 8 (The mains coil), task text and card title
findings.what: It calls lesson 6's screen 6 load "lesson 6's coil" and says "the resistor part reads 200 V", but lesson 6 drew a separate resistor and coil in series with the resistor's own meter, and a single real coil has no resistor part to meter, so name it lesson 6's resistor and coil in series.

findings.where: screen 7 (Ohms to watts), opening frames of the triangle
findings.what: The starting impedance triangle is drawn at a quarter of its final size (sides of about 10, 14 and 18 drawing units, mostly arrowheads), so lesson 6's 6-8-10 triangle reads as a small blob under its three labels before it grows; draw this screen at a larger scale so the ohms triangle is recognisable before it becomes the power triangle.

findings.where: screen 1 opening state at 0°, power triangle labels (360 light)
findings.what: With the triangle lying flat, "S = 500 VA" and "Q = 0 var" sit on one line with a small gap and read as one run of text; move Q's label clear of S's when Q is zero.

findings.where: screens 1 to 5 in dark mode, the light shading and its key swatch (360 dark, screen 2)
findings.what: The light shading for "energy back to the supply" (fill-opacity 0.14) nearly disappears on the dark background, in the dips and in its key swatch, so the returned energy, the lesson's central sight, is faint; raise its strength in dark mode.
The answer rests on "the wave swings as far above its average as below it", which screen 1 shows but no screen argues until screen 3's split, so add a pointer such as "screen 3 shows why".

"The current stops at 60° either way" gives no reason; one clause (nearer 90° the current needed for 500 W grows without limit, already 27.3 A rms at 75°) would turn the drawing's limit into the lesson's point.
Unlike the other puzzles, its wrong picks (500 var, 250 var) draw nothing in red; a red upright of 500 or 250 var on the flat triangle would show the slip the way the other screens do.

Nothing on the current wave shows it can be grabbed (the drag area is invisible), so on a phone Dan will reach for the slider; a small handle or a short cue on the dashed wave would show him he can move the thing that causes the dip.
